You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. paragraphs.sourceText: Many men and women have long bought into the idea that there are “male” and “female” brains, believing that explains just about every difference between the sexes. A new study 26 that belief, questioning whether brains really can be distinguished by gender.
paragraphs.translationZh: 许多男人和女人长期以来都相信大脑有“男性”和“女性”之分，相信这几乎可以解释两性之间的所有差异。一项新的研究挑战了这一信念，质疑大脑是否真的可以通过性别来区分。

paragraphs.sourceText: In the study, Tel Aviv University researchers 27 for sex differences the entire human brain.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在这项研究中，特拉维夫大学的研究人员在整个人类大脑中寻找性别差异。

paragraphs.sourceText: And what did they find? Not much. Rather than offer evidence for 28 brains as “male” or “female,” research shows that brains fall into a wide range, with most people falling right in the middle.
paragraphs.translationZh: 他们发现了什么？不多。研究表明，大脑的分类范围很广，大多数人都处于中间位置，而不是提供证据将大脑分为“男性”或“女性”。

paragraphs.sourceText: Daphna Joel, who led the study, said her research found that while there are some gender-based 29 , many different types of brain can't always be distinguished by gender.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这项研究的领导者达夫娜·乔尔表示，她的研究发现，虽然存在一些基于性别的相似性，但许多不同类型的大脑并不总是能通过性别来区分。

paragraphs.sourceText: While the “average” male and “average” female brains were 30 different, you couldn't tell it by looking at individual brain scans. Only a small 31 of people had “all-male” or “all-female” characteristics.
paragraphs.translationZh: 虽然“平均”男性和“平均”女性的大脑略有不同，但你无法通过查看单个脑部扫描来辨别这一点。只有一小部分人具有“全男性”或“全女性”特征。

paragraphs.sourceText: Larry Cahill, an American neuroscientist（神经科学家）, said the study is an important addition to a growing body of research questioning 32 beliefs about gender and brain function. But he cautioned against concluding from this study that all brains are the same, 33 of gender.
paragraphs.translationZh: 美国神经科学家拉里·卡希尔 (Larry Cahill) 表示，这项研究是对越来越多质疑性别和大脑功能传统观念的研究的重要补充。但他警告不要从这项研究中得出“无论性别如何，所有大脑都是相同的”的结论。

paragraphs.sourceText: “There's a mountain of evidence 34 the importance of sex influences at all levels of brain function,” he told The Seattle Times.
paragraphs.translationZh: “有大量证据证明性别对大脑各个层面功能的重要性，”他告诉《西雅图时报》。

paragraphs.sourceText: If anything, he said, the study 35 that gender plays a very important role in the brain “even when we are not clear exactly how.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 他说，如果说有什么不同的话，那就是这项研究表明，性别在大脑中发挥着非常重要的作用，“即使我们不清楚到底如何发挥作用”。

paragraphs.sourceText: Can Burglars Jam Your Wireless Security System?
paragraphs.translationZh: 窃贼可以干扰您的无线安全系统吗？

paragraphs.sourceText: A. Any product that promises to protect your home deserves careful examination. So it isn't surprising that you'll find plenty of strong opinions about the potential vulnerabilities of popular home-security systems.
paragraphs.translationZh: 答：任何承诺保护您的家庭的产品都值得仔细检查。因此，您会发现许多关于流行家庭安全系统的潜在漏洞的强烈意见也就不足为奇了。

paragraphs.sourceText: B. The most likely type of burglary（入室盗窃）by far is the unsophisticated crime of opportunity, usually involving a broken window or some forced entry. According to the FBI, crimes like these accounted roughly two-thirds of all household burglaries in the US in 2013.The wide majority of the rest were illegal, unforced entries that resulted from something like a window being left open. The odds of a criminal using technical means to bypass a security system are so small that the FBI doesn't even track those statistics.
paragraphs.translationZh: B. 到目前为止，最有可能的入室盗窃类型是简单的机会犯罪，通常涉及打破窗户或强行入室。据联邦调查局 (FBI) 称，2013 年美国所有入室盗窃案中此类犯罪大约占三分之二。其余的绝大多数都是非法、非强制入室盗窃，例如窗户开着之类的原因。犯罪分子利用技术手段绕过安全系统的可能性非常小，以至于联邦调查局甚至不跟踪这些统计数据。

paragraphs.sourceText: C. One of the main theoretical home-security concerns is whether or not a given system is vulnerable to being blocked from working altogether. With wired setups, the fear is that a burglar（入室盗贼）might be able to shut your system down simply by cutting the right cable. With a wireless setup, you stick battery-powered sensors up around your home that keep an eye on windows, doors, motion, and more. If they detect something wrong while the system is armed, they'll transmit a wireless alert signal to a base station that will then raise the alarm. That approach will eliminate most cord-cutting concerns—but what about their wireless equivalent, jamming? With the right device tuned to the right frequency, what's to stop a thief from jamming your setup and blocking that alert signal from ever reaching the base station?
paragraphs.translationZh: C. 理论上家庭安全的主要关注点之一是给定系统是否容易被完全阻止工作。对于有线设置，人们担心窃贼可能只需剪断正确的电缆就可以关闭您的系统。通过无线设置，您可以将电池供电的传感器安装在家里周围，以监视窗户、门、运动等。如果他们在系统布防时检测到问题，就会向基站发送无线警报信号，然后基站发出警报。这种方法将消除大多数断线问题，但无线等效物干扰又如何呢？将正确的设备调到正确的频率后，如何才能阻止小偷干扰您的设置并阻止警报信号到达基站？

paragraphs.sourceText: D. Jamming concerns are nothing new, and they're not unique to security systems. Any device that's built to receive a wireless signal at a specific frequency can be overwhelmed by a stronger signal coming in on the same frequency. For comparison, let's say you wanted to “jam” a conversation between two people—all you'd need to do is yell in the listener's ear.
paragraphs.translationZh: D. 干扰问题并不是什么新鲜事，也不是安全系统所独有的。任何用于接收特定频率无线信号的设备都可能会被相同频率的更强信号淹没。为了进行比较，假设您想要“干扰”两个人之间的对话 - 您所需要做的就是在听众耳边大喊大叫。

paragraphs.sourceText: E. Security devices are required to list the frequencies they broadcast on—that means that a potential thief can find what they need to know with minimal Googling. They will, however, need so know what system they're looking for. If you have a sign in your yard declaring what setup you use, that'd point them in the right direction, though at that point, we're talking about a highly targeted, semi-sophisticated attack, and not the sort forced-entry attack that makes up the majority of burglaries. It's easier to find and acquire jamming equipment for some frequencies than it is for others.
paragraphs.translationZh: E. 安全设备需要列出它们广播的频率——这意味着潜在的窃贼只需很少的谷歌搜索就可以找到他们需要知道的信息。然而，他们需要知道他们正在寻找什么系统。如果你的院子里有一个标牌，说明你使用的设置，那就会给他们指明正确的方向，尽管此时，我们谈论的是高度针对性的、半复杂的攻击，而不是构成大多数入室盗窃的那种强行进入攻击。某些频率的干扰设备比其他频率的干扰设备更容易找到和获取。

paragraphs.sourceText: F. Wireless security providers will often take steps to help combat the threat of jamming attacks. SimpliSafe, winner of our Editor's Choice distinction, utilizes a special system that's capable of separating incidental RF interference from targeted jamming attacks. When the system thinks it's being jammed, it'll notify you via push alert （推送警报）. From there, it's up to you to sound the alarm manually.
paragraphs.translationZh: F. 无线安全提供商通常会采取措施来帮助应对干扰攻击的威胁。 SimpliSafe 是我们编辑选择奖的获奖者，它采用了一种特殊的系统，能够将偶然的射频干扰与有针对性的干扰攻击分开。当系统认为出现拥塞时，它会通过推送警报的方式通知您。从那里，您可以手动发出警报。

paragraphs.sourceText: G. SimpliSafe was singled out in one recent article on jamming, complete with a video showing the entire system being effectively bypassed with handheld jamming equipment. After taking appropriate measures to contain the RF interference to our test lab, we tested the attack out for ourselves, and were able to verify that it's possible with the right equipment. However, we also verified that SimpliSafe's anti-jamming system works. It caught us in the act, sent an alert to my smartphone, and also listed our RF interference on the system's event log. The team behind the article and video in question make no mention of the system, or whether or not in detected them.
paragraphs.translationZh: 最近一篇关于干扰的文章特别提到了 G. SimpliSafe，并附有一段视频，显示手持干扰设备有效地绕过了整个系统。在采取适当措施遏制对我们测试实验室的射频干扰后，我们亲自测试了这种攻击，并能够验证使用正确的设备是否可以实现这种攻击。不过，我们也验证了SimpliSafe的抗干扰系统的工作原理。它当场抓住了我们，向我的智能手机发送了警报，还在系统的事件日志中列出了我们的射频干扰。相关文章和视频背后的团队没有提及该系统，也没有提及是否检测到它们。

paragraphs.sourceText: H. We like the unique nature of that software. It means that a thief likely wouldn't be able to Google how the system works, then figure out a way around it. Even if they could, SimpliSafe claims that its system is always evolving, and that it varies slightly from system to system, which means there wouldn't be a universal magic formula for cracking it. Other systems also seem confident on the subject of jamming. The team at Frontpoint addresses the issue in a blog on its site, citing their own jam protection software and claiming that there aren't any documented cases of successful jam attack since the company began offering wireless security sensors in the 1980s.
paragraphs.translationZh: H. 我们喜欢该软件的独特性。这意味着窃贼可能无法通过谷歌搜索系统的工作原理，然后找出解决方法。即使他们可以，SimpliSafe 声称它的系统总是在不断发展，并且每个系统的系统略有不同，这意味着不存在破解它的通用魔法公式。其他系统似乎对干扰问题也充满信心。 Frontpoint 团队在其网站的博客中解决了这个问题，引用了他们自己的拥塞保护软件，并声称自该公司在 20 世纪 80 年代开始提供无线安全传感器以来，没有任何成功的拥塞攻击的记录案例。

paragraphs.sourceText: I. Jamming attacks are absolutely possible. As said before, with the right equipment and the right know-how, it's possible to jam any wireless transmission. But how probable is it that someone will successfully jam their way into your home and steal your stuff?
paragraphs.translationZh: 一、干扰攻击是绝对有可能的。如前所述，只要有正确的设备和正确的专业知识，就有可能干扰任何无线传输。但是，有人成功闯入您家并偷走您的东西的可能性有多大？

paragraphs.sourceText: J. Let's imagine that you live in a small home with a wireless security setup that offers a functional anti-jamming system. First, a thief is going to need to target your home, specifically. Then, he's going to need to know the technical details of your system and acquire the specific equipment necessary for jamming your specific setup. Presumably, you keep your doors locked at night and while you're away. So the thief will still need to break in. That means defeating the lock somehow, or breaking a window. He'll need to be jamming you at this point, as a broken window or opened door would normally release the alarm. So, too, would the motion detectors in your home, so the thief will need to continue jamming once he's inside and searching for things to steal. However, he'll need to do so without tripping the anti-jamming system, the details of which he almost certainly does now have access to.
paragraphs.translationZh: J. 让我们想象一下，您住在一个小房子里，配有无线安全设置，可提供功能性抗干扰系统。首先，小偷需要专门瞄准您的家。然后，他需要了解您的系统的技术细节，并获取干扰您的特定设置所需的特定设备。想必，您在晚上和外出时都会锁好门。所以小偷仍然需要破门而入。这意味着以某种方式破解锁，或者打破窗户。他需要在这个时候干扰你，因为打破的窗户或打开的门通常会触发警报。你家中的运动探测器也是如此，因此小偷一旦进入室内并寻找可偷的东西，就需要继续干扰。然而，他需要在不触发抗干扰系统的情况下这样做，他现在几乎肯定可以访问该系统的详细信息。

paragraphs.sourceText: K. At the end of the day, these kinds of systems are primarily designed to protect against the sort of opportunistic smash-and-grab attack that makes up the majority of burglaries. They're also only a single layer in what should ideally be a many-sided approach to securing your home, one that includes common sense things like sound locks and proper exterior lighting at night. No system is impenetrable, and none can promise to eliminate the worst case completely. Every one of them has vulnerabilities that a knowledgeable thief could theoretically exploit. A good system is one that keeps that worst-case setting as improbable as possible while also offering strong protection in the event of a less-extraordinary attack.
paragraphs.translationZh: K. 归根结底，此类系统的主要设计目的是防止大多数入室盗窃中的机会主义砸抢攻击。它们也只是理想情况下保护您的房屋的多方面方法中的一层，其中包括常识性的东西，例如隔音锁和夜间适当的外部照明。没有一个系统是坚不可摧的，也没有一个系统可以承诺完全消除最坏的情况。它们中的每一个都存在漏洞，理论上，知识渊博的窃贼可以利用这些漏洞。一个好的系统能够尽可能避免出现最坏的情况，同时在发生不太特殊的攻击时提供强有力的保护。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. It is possible for burglars to make jamming attacks with the necessary equipment and skill.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 窃贼有可能利用必要的设备和技能进行干扰攻击。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. Interfering with a wireless security system is similar to interfering with a conversation.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 干扰无线安全系统类似于干扰谈话。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. A burglar has to continuously jam the wireless security device to avoid triggering the alarm, both inside and outside the house.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 窃贼必须在屋内和屋外不断干扰无线安全装置以避免触发警报。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. SimpliSafe provides devices that are able to distinguish incidental radio interference from targeted jamming attacks.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. SimpliSafe 提供能够区分偶然无线电干扰和有针对性的干扰攻击的设备。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. Only a very small proportion of burglaries are committed by technical means.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 只有极少数入室盗窃是通过技术手段实施的。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. It is difficult to crack SimpliSafe as its system keeps changing.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. SimpliSafe 的系统不断变化，因此很难破解。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. Wireless devices will transmit signals so as to activate the alarm once something wrong is detected.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 一旦检测到问题，无线设备将传输信号以启动警报。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. Different measures should be taken to protect one's home from burglary in addition to the wireless security system.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 除了无线安全系统外，还应采取不同措施来保护住宅免遭盗窃。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. SimpliSafe's device can send a warning to the house owner's cellphone.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. SimpliSafe 的设备可以向房主的手机发送警告。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. Burglars can easily get a security device's frequency by Internet search.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45.窃贼可以通过互联网搜索轻松获得安全设备的频率。

For each of them there are four choices marked A),B),C) and D).You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: As a person who writes about food and drink for a living. I couldn't tell you the first thing about Bill Perry or whether the beers he sells are that great. But I can tell you that I like this guy. That's because he plans to ban tipping in favor of paying his servers an actual living wage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 作为一个以写食物和饮料为生的人。我无法告诉你有关比尔·佩里的第一件事，或者他销售的啤酒是否那么好。但我可以告诉你，我喜欢这个人。这是因为他计划禁止给小费，转而向服务员支付实际生活工资。

paragraphs.sourceText: I hate tipping.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我讨厌给小费。

paragraphs.sourceText: I hate it because it's an obligation disguised as an option. I hate it for the post-dinner math it requires of me. But mostly, I hate tipping because I believe I would be in a better place if pay decisions regarding employees were simply left up to their employers, as is the custom in virtually every other industry.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我讨厌它，因为这是一种伪装成选择的义务。我讨厌它，因为它要求我做饭后数学。但最重要的是，我讨厌给小费，因为我相信，如果员工的薪酬决定完全由雇主决定，就像几乎所有其他行业的惯例一样，我会处于一个更好的位置。

paragraphs.sourceText: Most of you probably think that you hate tipping, too. Research suggests otherwise. You actually love tipping! You like to feel that you have a voice in how much money your server makes. No matter how the math works out, you persistently view restaurants with voluntary tipping systems as being a better value, which makes it extremely difficult for restaurants and bars to do away with the tipping system.
paragraphs.translationZh: 大多数人可能认为自己也讨厌给小费。研究表明情况并非如此。你其实很喜欢给小费！您喜欢感觉自己对服务器赚多少钱有发言权。无论计算结果如何，您始终认为采用自愿小费系统的餐厅更有价值，这使得餐馆和酒吧很难取消小费系统。

paragraphs.sourceText: One argument that you tend to hear a lot from the pro-tipping crowd seems logical enough: the service is better when waiters depend on tips, presumably because they see a benefit to successfully veiling their contempt for you. Well, if this were true, we would all be slipping a few 100-dollar bills to our doctors on the way out their doors, too. But as it turns out, waiters see only a tiny bump in tips when they do an exceptional job compared to a passable one. Waiters, keen observers of humanity that they are, are catching on to this; in one poll, a full 30% said they didn't believe the job they did had any impact on the tips they received.
paragraphs.translationZh: 您经常从赞成给小费的人群中听到的一种论点似乎很合乎逻辑：当服务员依赖小费时，服务会更好，大概是因为他们看到了成功掩饰对您的蔑视的好处。好吧，如果这是真的，我们也会在出门时给医生塞几张 100 美元的钞票。但事实证明，当服务员做得非常出色时，与表现还过得去的服务员相比，他们得到的小费只会有微小的增加。服务员作为人性的敏锐观察者，正在意识到这一点。在一项民意调查中，整整 30% 的人表示，他们不相信自己所做的工作对他们收到的小费有任何影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: So come on, folks: get on board with ditching the outdated tip system. Pay a little more upfront for your beer or burger. Support Bill Perry's pub, and any other bar or restaurant that doesn't ask you to do drunken math.
paragraphs.translationZh: 所以，来吧，伙计们：放弃过时的小费系统吧。为啤酒或汉堡多付一点钱。支持比尔·佩里的酒吧，以及任何其他不要求你做醉酒数学的酒吧或餐厅。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: In the past, falling oil prices have given a boost to the world economy, but recent forecasts for global growth have been toned down, even as oil prices sink lower and lower. Does that mean the link between lower oil prices and growth has weakened?
paragraphs.translationZh: 过去，油价下跌曾提振世界经济，但最近对全球经济增长的预测有所下调，尽管油价越来越低。这是否意味着油价下跌与经济增长之间的联系已经减弱？

paragraphs.sourceText: Some experts say there are still good reasons to believe cheap oil should heat up the world economy. Consumers have more money in their pockets when they're paying less at the pump. They spend that money on other things, which stimulates the economy.
paragraphs.translationZh: 一些专家表示，仍然有充分的理由相信廉价石油应该会提振世界经济。当消费者在加油时支付更少的费用时，他们的口袋里就会有更多的钱。他们把钱花在其他事情上，从而刺激经济。

paragraphs.sourceText: The biggest gains go to countries that import most of their oil like China, Japan, and India, But doesn't the extra money in the pockets of those countries' consumers mean an equal loss in oil producing countries, cancelling out the gains? Not necessarily, says economic researcher Sara Johnson. “Many oil producers built up huge reserve funds when prices were high, so when prices fall they will draw on their reserves to support government spending and subsidies(补贴)for their consumers.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 最大的收益归于中国、日本和印度等石油进口最多的国家，但这些国家消费者口袋里的额外钱是否意味着石油生产国同样遭受损失，抵消了收益？经济研究员萨拉·约翰逊表示，不一定。 “许多石油生产国在价格高位时建立了巨额储备基金，因此当价格下跌时，他们将动用储备金来支持政府支出和对消费者的补贴。”

paragraphs.sourceText: But not all oil producers have big reserves, In Venezuela, collapsing oil prices have sent its economy into free-fall.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但并非所有石油生产国都拥有大量储备。在委内瑞拉，油价暴跌导致其经济直线下滑。

paragraphs.sourceText: Economist Carl Weinberg believes the negative effects of plunging oil prices are overwhelming the positive effects of cheaper oil. The implication is a sharp decline in global trade, which has plunged partly because oil-producing nations can't afford to import as much as they used to.
paragraphs.translationZh: 经济学家卡尔·温伯格认为，油价暴跌的负面影响压倒了油价下跌的正面影响。这意味着全球贸易急剧下降，部分原因是产油国无法像以前那样进口那么多石油。

paragraphs.sourceText: Sara Johnson acknowledges that the global economic benefit from a fall in oil prices today is likely lower than it was in the past. One reason is that more countries are big oil producers now, so the nations suffering from the price drop account for a larger share of the global economy.
paragraphs.translationZh: 萨拉·约翰逊承认，当今油价下跌带来的全球经济利益可能低于过去。原因之一是现在越来越多的国家成为石油生产大国，因此遭受油价下跌的国家在全球经济中所占的份额更大。

paragraphs.sourceText: Consumers, in the U.S. at least, are acting cautiously with the savings they're getting at the gas pump, as the memory of the recent great recession is still fresh in their mind. And a number of oil-producing countries are trimming their gasoline subsidies and raising taxes, so the net savings for global consumers is not as big as the oil price plunge might suggest.
paragraphs.translationZh: 至少在美国，消费者对加油时节省的钱持谨慎态度，因为他们对最近的经济大衰退记忆犹新。一些产油国正在削减汽油补贴并提高税收，因此全球消费者的净储蓄并不像油价暴跌所暗示的那么大。
